LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 HAND WRITING BRAILLE WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing Braille Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing Braille Writing, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we write words and sentences neatly and legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing Braille Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to write clearly and correctly is enhanced as they write words in clear and legible

handwriting or braille writing.

• Digital literacy: The learner’s ability to create with technology is improved as they type words and phrases on digital devices with assistive

technology.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates the effort of peers to write correctly and assist those with writing difficulties.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learner Support Programmes (Peer Education and Mentorship): The learner’s ability to mentor others is developed as they model good handwriting to

their peers.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner uses the handwriting skills or braille skills to learn similar concept in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
